raw_candidate_set.title: Single-pass coefficient coverage
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: A local loop-invariant check can target the fact that mlk_poly_add executes one zero-based loop from i = 0 to i < MLKEM_N, so each coefficient position 0..255 is visited exactly once and the loop is bounded by MLKEM_N.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: for (i = 0; i < MLKEM_N; i++) { r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i]); }
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The function uses one simple for-loop over the coefficient array.
The loop bound constant is 256 in the provided snapshot.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: All arrays have indices that begin at zero.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: Zero-based indexing is the specification convention used to interpret the loop indices.

required_assumptions: mlk_poly objects are well-formed and expose MLKEM_N accessible coefficients.
The loop executes as written without external jumps or macro side effects.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not claim semantic correctness of the arithmetic update.
Does not establish any modular-q property.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: No caller context or loop contract is visible, so the property is limited to the local loop structure.
limitations: The body does not document behavior for invalid pointers.
This is a coverage/termination property, not a functional equivalence claim.

raw_candidate_set.title: Writes confined to destination coefficient array
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: A frame check can target the fact that the only visible writes are to r->coeffs[i] for i in [0, MLKEM_N), with no allocation, deallocation, or explicit global-state update in the body.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The only visible write target is the destination coefficient array.
The API exposes a mutable destination pointer and a const-qualified source pointer.

required_assumptions: The visible function body is complete for this symbol.
No hidden macro expansion introduces extra side effects.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not assert that b remains semantically unchanged under pointer aliasing.
Does not rule out shared-memory effects if r and b alias the same object.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The snapshot does not include aliasing or ownership contracts.
limitations: Semantic effects through aliasing are not ruled out.
This is a local footprint observation, not a whole-function proof.

raw_candidate_set.title: Same-index coefficient update expression
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: A functional check can target the exact per-iteration update expression r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i]) with same-index reads from r and b and a same-index write back to r.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The update uses the current coefficient from each operand at the same index.
The storage layout is a fixed-length coefficient array of int16_t values.

required_assumptions: Standard C integer promotion and narrowing-cast semantics are used in the verifier model.
No undefined behavior is introduced by an unseen wrapper or macro path.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not claim the result equals modular addition in Z_q.
Does not by itself establish any caller-side alias policy.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The source snapshot does not show a modular reduction step or a contract that connects the cast to ring semantics.
limitations: If later reasoning needs a ring-level postcondition, additional invariants will be required.
The property is local to each iteration and does not address semantic aliasing separately.

raw_candidate_set.title: Canonical-input range safety for the cast
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: A range check can target the fact that, if both input coefficients are canonical ML-KEM residues in [0, q-1] with q = 3329, then each sum r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i] lies in [0, 6656], which fits in int16_t before the cast.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: q denotes the prime integer 3329 ... elements of R_q are represented as arrays in Z_q^256.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: Canonical ML-KEM coefficients are residues modulo q in the range 0..q-1.
The destination storage type is signed 16-bit integers.
The visible update performs addition followed by a cast to int16_t.

required_assumptions: Both operands are already canonical representatives in Z_q.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not imply the result is reduced modulo q or canonicalized.
Does not establish the function’s full mathematical correctness.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The source snapshot does not state any precondition that inputs are canonical residues, so the range claim is conditional.
limitations: The property is about cast safety, not about modular equivalence.
A later proof would still need an external input-shape assumption.

raw_candidate_set.title: No explicit local q-reduction in the visible body
raw_candidate_set.candidate_statement: A semantic-gap check can target the absence of explicit q-reduction in the visible body: there is no MLKEM_Q use, modulus operator, or reduction helper call, so any modular-q interpretation must come from external invariants or surrounding code rather than this body alone.

supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The visible body shows only addition and a cast, with no explicit modulo reduction.
The q constant exists in the snapshot but is not referenced by the visible body.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: z <- x + y means that z is assigned the value x + y mod m.
supporting_evidence.supports_claim: The specification's abstract arithmetic semantics are modular, which highlights the gap between spec-level semantics and the visible body.

required_assumptions: The provided body is complete and not conditionally expanded into additional reduction code.
No hidden helper invoked by macro expansion is omitted.
out_of_scope_boundaries: Does not claim the wider project fails to normalize coefficients elsewhere.
Does not claim a verified mismatch between code and specification.
raw_candidate_set.uncertainty: The absence of an explicit mod step is visible, but the broader representation invariant is not.
limitations: This is a discovery about visible code shape, not a proof that modular semantics are absent from the overall implementation.
It is narrower than a full algebraic correctness claim.
